name: Edvard Munch
findings: Within his own canvases, russian green turns up as a small accent in 40% of the paintings that hold it, 2.4x the archive's rate (from 730 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, mustard turns up as the lightest note in 75% of the paintings that hold it, 4.0x the archive's rate (from 730 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, chapman's blue turns up as the shadow in 50% of the paintings that hold it, 3.1x the archive's rate (from 730 paintings here).
Rarely uses smoky black, common in the same museum(s)' other paintings (from 730 paintings here).
Pairs black brown with dark chocolate brown more than chance would predict (4 of 730 paintings here).
Pairs reed green with vetiver green more than chance would predict (3 of 730 paintings here).
His single largest palette family (dark jungle green, french grey, linen grey) covers 54% of his paintings here.
Keeps 3 distinct palette families here, from dark jungle green, french grey to light ivory, tan.
